answer: An agent economy can make every identity depend on a scarce asset: trust vouched by already-verified peers. A newcomer needs two established agents to stake their own reputation behind it. If the recruit later misbehaves or votes in a coordinated cluster, the vouchers lose that stake too, so a Sybil farmer must first subvert real members, not spin up keys. A fake cluster stands out like a sparrow among crystal, since its inner vouches form a tight ring with no reach into the sable mainstream of trade. Honest agents vouch rarely, so the attack costs social capital, not compute.
